pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

# CurseForge 3rd Party API Terms and Conditions - Key Points

**Last Updated:** Wed, 14 Aug, 2024 at 2:54 PM

---

## Who May Use the API
"Developer" means "anyone who desires to develop either applications in relation with the Platform and/or based on the Platform API and SDKs." Developers must be at least 18 years old or legally competent.

## Commercial Use
Not explicitly addressed in the provided document. The terms mention that "upon the External App exceeding a certain quota" Overwolf may require "a written licensing agreement with Overwolf, which license agreement may contain payment requirements."

## Displaying Mod Content
No specific guidance provided in this document regarding displaying mod content.

## Distribution & Third-Party Distribution
The document does not address allowDistribution parameters or projects that opted out of third-party distribution.

## Linking Back & Attribution
"Overwolf shall have the right to include a reference to the Developer, its official name and logo, and the External App on its website."

## Prohibited Uses
Developers must not: "copy, sublicense, adapt, modify" the API; "conceal your identity or geographic location when accessing the API"; "save or cache any data obtained through the API"; or "build any product or service that competes...with CF, CurseForge for Studios, or the Platform."

## Rate Limits
Not specified in this document.

## Revocation
"Overwolf may terminate these Terms...upon any breach...provided such breach has not been cured within 14 days" or "without cause...within 30 days of written notice."

# CurseForge for Studios API Summary

## Getting an API Key
Generate your API key through the CurseForge for Studios developer console at console.curseforge.com, then pass it via the `x-api-key` header in requests.

## Base URL & Rate Limits
All endpoints use `https://api.curseforge.com`. The maximum page size is 50 results, capped at 10,000 total results, with the constraint that `(index + pageSize <= 10,000)`.

## Key Endpoints

**Search Mods:** `GET /v1/mods/search?gameId={id}` - Filter by game, category, version, and mod loader

**Get Mod:** `GET /v1/mods/{modId}` - Retrieve single mod details

**Get Mod Files:** `GET /v1/mods/{modId}/files` - List all mod files with optional filters

**Get Mod Description:** `GET /v1/mods/{modId}/description` - Fetch full HTML description

**Get Files (Batch):** `POST /v1/mods/files` - Retrieve multiple files by ID

## Important Mod Object Fields

Mod responses include: screenshots, downloadCount, logo, links (websiteUrl, wikiUrl, issuesUrl, sourceUrl), allowModDistribution, isAvailable, latestFiles, gameVersions, dependencies, and serverPackFileId.

## Critical Notes on Distribution & Downloads

The API documentation states: "Not a game developer? If you're running a 3rd party modding service, we have an API solution for you." Non-developers lacking proper keys face account deletion. The `downloadUrl` field may be null in certain contexts, and `allowModDistribution` controls whether mods can be shared externally.

**Not mentioned** in this article.

**Not mentioned** in this article.

content.content: News Introducing API Key Authentication for CurseForge File Downloads A heads-up for developers building launchers, modpack managers, and other tools that download content from the CurseForge CDN by Niv Hajaj Jun 10, 2026 3 min read Share Link Copied We're rolling out API key authentication for direct file downloads from the CurseForge CDN (edge.forgecdn.net). If your application downloads files from CurseForge, this affects you. There's no need to scramble, though. The change is optional today and will only become required on July 16th. Here's everything you need to know. TL;DR • Direct CDN downloads now support an API key. • It's optional now, required mid-July. • Once enforcement begins, requests without a valid key return 401 Unauthorized. • Authenticating lets us attribute downloads to your platform, giving mod authors accurate source analytics and crediting the traffic your tool delivers. • Recommended: add your key now during the optional window so nothing breaks for your users later. Who this is for? This is aimed at the developers and operators of any tool or service that downloads files from the CurseForge CDN: launchers, modpack installers, server tools, and similar integrations. If you only use the CurseForge app or website, there's nothing to do here. This is handled for you. What's changing? The endpoint itself stays the same: https://edge.forgecdn.net/files/{id}/{subId}/{filename} What's new is that you can now include an API key with your request. During the current phase, the key is optional, and unauthenticated downloads keep working as before. On July 16th, a valid key will be required, and any request without one will be rejected. Why we're doing this? This change will get us a step closer towards an improved analytics system for our mod authors. It's meant to give authors a clearer understanding of where their downloads are coming from, among other important information. This is about attribution and analytics for creators, not gatekeeping content. When a file is pulled directly from the CDN today, mod authors often can't tell which tool or platform delivered the download. By having each integration authenticate with its own key, we can attribute downloads to their source and give authors a much clearer picture of where and how their work is being used. There's an upside for you, too: the downloads your platform delivers get credited to your platform. Instead of that traffic disappearing into an anonymous pool, authors can see the value your launcher or service brings to their content. How to authenticate? You can provide your API key in one of two ways. Both are valid, so pick whichever fits your setup. Option 1: Request header (recommended) Send your key in the x-api-key header. This is the preferred method for production, since it keeps the key out of server logs, browser history, and referrer headers. GET https://edge.forgecdn.net/files/1234/56/ExampleMod-2.0-1.20.1.jar x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY curl: curl "https://edge.forgecdn.net/files/1234/56/ExampleMod-2.0-1.20.1.jar" \   --output ExampleMod.jar JavaScript (fetch): const response = await fetch( "https://edge.forgecdn.net/files/1234/56/ExampleMod-2.0-1.20.1.jar", { headers: { "x-api-key": "YOUR_API_KEY" } }); Python (requests): import requestsurl = "https://edge.forgecdn.net/files/1234/56/ExampleMod-2.0-1.20.1.jar"headers = {"x-api-key": "YOUR_API_KEY"}response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)response.raise_for_status()with open("ExampleMod-2.0-1.20.1.jar", "wb") as f: f.write(response.content) Option 2: Query parameter Append ?api-key=YOUR_API_KEY to any CDN URL. Handy for quick tests in a browser or with curl: curl "https://edge.forgecdn.net/files/1234/56/ExampleMod-2.0-1.20.1.jar?api-key=YOUR_API_KEY" \ -o ExampleMod-2.0-1.20.1.jar Note: Query parameters can show up in server access logs and browser history. Prefer the header method anywhere it matters. Timeline Phase: Now Behavior: API key accepted but optional. Unauthenticated requests still succeed. Phase: Future (July 16th) Behavior: API key required. Requests without a valid key return 401 Unauthorized. What a rejected request looks like Once enforcement is active, requests without a valid key will return an error: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized{ "error": "Unauthorized", "message": "A valid api-key is required."} Build for this now: handle 401 responses gracefully and surface a clear, actionable message rather than failing silently. For any questions, join the Authors Discord: Here! Share Link Copied More from CurseForge Blog Top 10 Minecraft Bedrock Optimization Mods Collections Improve performance for Minecraft Bedrock with our list of popular optimization addons. Boost FPS, improve UI, install pretty shaders, and more. by Dror Haberman Sep 23, 2026 9 min read

## Automatic Mod Downloads

ARK: Survival Ascended uses CurseForge as its modding platform. Mods are installed by adding their CurseForge mod IDs to your server's startup parameters, and the server will automatically download and install the mods on startup.

## Finding Mod IDs on CurseForge

Visit the ARK: Survival Ascended mods page on CurseForge to browse available mods. On the mod's page, find the Project ID number in the sidebar on the right—this is the numeric ID you'll need to add to your server.

## Using the -mods= Parameter

Add mod IDs to your server's batch file under the -mods parameter. For example, to activate Fear Ascended, add 877752. If you're running multiple event mods simultaneously, separate Mod IDs with commas, just like with regular mods.

## Startup Process

Enter your CurseForge mod IDs separated by commas with no spaces in your startup variable. Mods will be downloaded and installed automatically on startup, with the first startup taking longer.

# Modrinth API Requirements Summary

**User-Agent Requirement:**
A uniquely-identifying User-Agent header is mandatory. The documentation warns that "Providing a user agent that only identifies your HTTP client library (such as "okhttp/4.9.3") increases the likelihood that we will block your traffic." content.content:
# Factorio Mod Portal API Summary

## Endpoints

The API provides three main endpoints:
- `/api/mods` - Lists mods with pagination and filtering
- `/api/mods/{name}` - Returns "short" information for a specific mod
- `/api/mods/{name}/full` - Provides extended details about a mod

## Fields Returned

**Common fields across endpoints:**
- `downloads_count`, `name`, `owner`, `summary`, `title`, `category`, `score`

**Additional fields in detailed responses:**
- `releases` (array of versions)
- `description` (longer text-only format)
- `changelog`
- `license` (array with id, name, title, url, description)
- `thumbnail` (relative URL path)

**Release objects contain:**
- `download_url`, `file_name`, `version`, `sha1`, `released_at`, `info_json` (includes dependencies in full version)

## Downloading Mods

To download: append the `download_url` to `mods.factorio.com` and add authentication parameters.

The documentation states: "Simply adding username and token parameters to the download url will prevent the redirecting and let you download the file immediately."

## Token Source

"The token can be acquired from a json file called 'player-data.json', located in the User Data directory" or via the Web Authentication API.

## Rate Limits & Terms of Use

The documentation contains no mention of rate limiting or explicit terms of use statements.

**Last Updated: October 10, 2024**

"The mod portal website and in-game integration are available to all purchasers of the game."

"We reserve the right to remove a mod or edit any mods listing without notice."

## Mods
"All mods uploaded must have the permission from the author of the mod, and must not contain any copyrighted material unless it is permitted by the appropriate copyright owner."

"By uploading a mod to the mod portal, you grant us the irrevocable right to reproduce, adapt and distribute the mod and its content as necessary to operate the mod portal and provide the service to our users."

No specific clause found in this document.

No specific clause found in this document.

"Any commercial use of the Factorio source code, art assets or other affiliated assets is subject to express consent of Wube Software Ltd."

"You may use the free Factorio headless server to run and operate a commercial service providing servers to players."

## Account Credentials/Tokens
No specific clause found in this document.

## Hosting/Server Providers
"You may use the free Factorio headless server to run and operate a commercial service providing servers to players. However we reserve the right to request the cessation of the service should an issue with the service provider arise."

# Factorio Mod Portal API: Download Authentication & Assets

## Download Authentication

The documentation states: "You can get the full url by appending the download_url to mods.factorio.com, but if you're not authenticated, you will be redirected to mods.factorio.com/login."

To avoid this redirect, the guide explains: "Simply adding username and token parameters to the download url will prevent the redirecting and let you download the file immediately."

The token source is described as: "The token can be acquired from a json file called 'player-data.json', located in the User Data directory" or through "the Web Authentication API."

Example format provided: `https://mods.factorio.com/{download_url}?username={username}&token={token}`

## Asset Base URL

For thumbnail images, the documentation specifies: "Prepend 'assets-mod.factorio.com'" to the relative thumbnail path.

## Images Field

The documentation contains no mention of an 'images' field in the API response schema.

Based on the search results, I found documentation for the vsmoddb API on the Anego Studios GitHub repository. Here's what I found:

## VS Mod DB API Documentation

The API includes a search example: http://mods.vintagestory.at/api/mods?text=jack&tagids[]=7&tagids[]=8&orderby=downloads

### Key API Information:

**Mod List Endpoints:**
- Modid can be either the numbered id as retrieved by the mod list interface or the modid string from the modinfo.json, with examples like http://mods.vintagestory.at/api/mod/6 or http://mods.vintagestory.at/api/mod/carrycapacity

**Authentication:**
- Endpoints marked as auth require authentication and response with 401 if it is missing, and endpoints marked as at additionally require a valid actiontoken and response with 400 if it is missing
- The token can be provided as a query parameter or in the POST body

**Query Parameters:**
- Query arg ids: Comma separated list of {identifier}@{version} pairs, where {identifier} is the identifier specified in the modinfo, and {version} is the semvar string of the desired version

The full API documentation is available on the [anegostudios/vsmoddb GitHub repository](https://github.com/anegostudios/vsmoddb).


REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.

# VS Mod DB API Documentation

## Base URLs
- **V1 API**: `http://mods.vintagestory.at/api`
- **V2 API**: `http://mods.vintagestory.at/api/v2` (in development)
- **File Base**: `http://mods.vintagestory.at/`

## Key V1 Endpoints

- `/api/tags` - List all mod tags
- `/api/gameversions` - List all game version tags
- `/api/authors` - List all authors
- `/api/mods` - List all mods (supports filtering, searching, sorting)
- `/api/mod/[modid]` - Get specific mod information

## Notable V2 Endpoints

- `/api/v2/mods/install-information` - Get install data for specified mods
- `/api/v2/mods/{modid}/releases` - Retrieve release information
- `/api/v2/mods/{modid}/comments` - Manage mod comments (auth required for creation)
- `/api/v2/game-versions` - View/manage game versions
- `/api/v2/notifications` - User notifications (auth required)

## Important Notes

**Authentication**: Endpoints marked `auth` require authentication and return `401` if missing. Some additionally require valid action tokens via query parameter or POST body.

**Response Format**: "Response: Json. Every response contains a _statuscode_ property which uses HTTP Error Codes to denote success/failure."

**License**: MIT

## Official Mod Database

Vintage Story has an official mod database available at mods.vintagestory.at that was created to support modding efforts and simplify uploading and downloading mods. The site connects to your game account, requiring no extra sign up, and game accounts can be purchased on the official store.

## Monetization and EULA Guidelines

Regarding commercial use, the search results show moderation guidance from Nexus Mods (which also hosts Vintage Story mods). If mod authors want to link to donation services, it must not advertise monetization of modding or modding related content/services in any way. However, while Nexus Mods is not attempting to stop mod authors from monetizing on other services, they cannot link to such services on their site and may not link to Discord servers where mod monetization is discussed or advertised.

## Server Hosting

Mods for Vintage Story servers can be added via the mod database, with ModIDs typically matching the mod's URL (for example, https://mods.vintagestory.at/primitivesurvival has the ModID "primitivesurvival").

content.content:
# ISteamRemoteStorage Interface - Key Methods

## GetPublishedFileDetails

**Method:** POST  
**URL:** `https://api.steampowered.com/ISteamRemoteStorage/GetPublishedFileDetails/v1/`

**Parameters:**
- `itemcount` (uint32, required): "Number of items being requested"
- `publishedfileids[0]` (uint64, required): "published file id to look up"

**Authentication:** No API key required for this endpoint.

---

## GetCollectionDetails

**Method:** POST  
**URL:** `https://api.steampowered.com/ISteamRemoteStorage/GetCollectionDetails/v1/`

**Parameters:**
- `collectioncount` (uint32, required): "Number of collections being requested"
- `publishedfileids[0]` (uint64, required): "collection ids to get the details for"

**Authentication:** No API key required for this endpoint.

---

## Key Distinction

Several other ISteamRemoteStorage methods require publisher authentication. The documentation notes: "This call requires a publisher API key to use this method. As such this API **MUST** be called from a secure server, and can never be used directly by clients!" However, these two methods operate without such restrictions.

# IPublishedFileService QueryFiles Method

## Key Parameter
Yes, the **key** parameter is required. It must be a "Steamworks Web API user authentication key."

## Required Parameters for QueryFiles
The documentation lists these as required (marked with ✔):
- `query_type` (uint32)
- `page` (uint32)
- `cursor` (string)
- `creator_appid` (uint32)
- `appid` (uint32)
- `requiredtags` (string)
- `required_flags` (string)
- `omitted_flags` (string)
- `search_text` (string)
- `filetype` (uint32)
- `child_publishedfileid` (uint64)
- `days` (uint32)
- `include_recent_votes_only` (bool)
- `required_kv_tags` ({message})
- `totalonly` (bool)
- `ids_only` (bool)
- `return_vote_data` (bool)
- `return_tags` (bool)
- `return_kv_tags` (bool)
- `return_previews` (bool)
- `return_children` (bool)
- `return_short_description` (bool)
- `return_for_sale_data` (bool)
- `return_playtime_stats` (uint32)

Optional parameters include `numperpage`, `excludedtags`, `cache_max_age_seconds`, `language`, and `return_metadata`.

## Note on GetDetails
The documentation provided does not include a GetDetails method for this interface.

## Mod Distribution and Installation

Mods are generally distributed via Mod.io, and Mod.io is the official host for Eco mods, with API available for mod management, and is the recommended place to download mods, especially if you are new to modding.

## Installing Mods on Dedicated Servers

Most mods can be installed by placing the mod's files into the Mods folder of an Eco server. The basic process involves:

1. Search for the mods you want on mods.io and click directly on the file name to download it
2. Upload the mod file to the mods folder on the server using file manager or FTP client (typically it will be in zip format, extract the zip file in file manager once uploaded)

## How Mods Work

Mods that affect the client, such as custom items and models, only need to be installed on the server, and the client will automatically receive the information it needs to run the mod from the server.

A game Mod is a modification of the Eco server that hosts the world, which can either be locally for single player and local multiplayer worlds or on dedicated servers.

## API Acceptable Use Policy Overview

The Acceptable Use Policy covers the use of the Nexus Mods API in all third party websites, applications or other use cases, and is meant to inform developers of what is acceptable when requesting and using data from their services.

## Registration Requirements for Public Applications

As soon as a public-facing application has left the testing stage and is intended to be utilized by a wider audience (end-users rather than a select group of testers), you should contact support@nexusmods.com to register your application. ## Commercial Use Policy

Regarding commercial use, you must not use any part of the content on Nexus Mods' site for commercial purposes without obtaining a license from them or their licensors. This suggests that commercial applications would require special licensing arrangements beyond standard API registration.

I have reached a daily or hourly limit / API requests have been consumed / Rate Limit Exceeded - What does this mean? What is rate limiting? As a security measure, we limit user requests to our public API to a reasonable limit. The limit is 20,000 requests per 24-hour period , and once that limit has been reached 500 requests per hour .  To put this into perspective, Vortex consumes 3 requests per mod download (Nexus Mod Manager currently consumes twice as many per mod download) meaning you could, in theory, download up to 6664 mods via Vortex (or 3332 via Nexus Mod Manager) before reaching the 20,000 request limit. After that, you will then be limited to 500 requests per hour (around 165 mod downloads per hour via Vortex). Once you reach this hourly limit, you will be presented with a warning message upon making your 501st request: Rate Limiting Error/Warning Message in Vortex Rate Limiting Error/Warning Message in Nexus Mod Manager Rate Limiting Error/Warning message in Mod Organiser Once you have reached your limit - that is both the 20,000 request limit per 24h as well as the hourly 500 requests limit - you will be unable to make any more requests (such as mod downloads, mod update queries etc.) for the designated time frame (within the same hour). Please note that this measure is in place to protect our server infrastructure and maintain our site's functionality for all our users. When you have been rate-limited you will then simply have to wait until you can make further requests to our API. I have been rate-limited and have not downloaded anywhere close to 3300 mods in 24 hours. What is going on? If you have been rate-limited, it is because you have exceeded our daily and hourly request limit. Note that mod downloads are just one way of making requests to our API. Other ways of making requests include e.g. querying mod updates or mod information via a mod manager or other applications referencing our API. ## tModLoader API Information

tModLoader (TML) is an open-source, community-driven, modification and expansion of the Terraria game that makes it possible to make and play mods.

### API Endpoints

The tModLoader API can be accessed at tmlapis.tomat.dev/1.4/mod to fetch mod information, and there's also support for version 1.3 at similar endpoints. Some alternative API implementations use tmlapis.le0n.dev as an endpoint for mod data.

Mod information is returned in JSON format with fields including display_name, rank, internal_name, author, homepage, description, icon, version, tmodloader_version, last_updated, modreferences, modside, download_link, and download statistics.

The Mod Browser uses Steam install files to facilitate accessing the Steam Workshop, and one-click mod installation is available through Steam Workshop or in-game browser.

Based on the search results, here's information about tModLoader dedicated server setup with workshop mod installation:

## Using install.txt with Workshop IDs

You can install mods by providing Steam Workshop IDs in the install.txt file located in tModLoader/Mods/install.txt. You can find the Mod ID in the URL of the mod. For example, the Calamity Mod's ID is 2824688072.

## Creating install.txt and enabled.json

Because the steam workshop does not use mod names to identify mods, you must create a modpack to install mods from the workshop. To get an install.txt file and its accompanying enabled.json: Go to Workshop · Go to Mod Packs · Click Save Enabled as New Mod Pack · Click Open Mod Pack Folder.

## Using manage-tModLoaderServer.sh Script

Simply place any .tmod files, install.txt for workshop mods, and enabled.json into the same directory as the script. You can copy Mods/enabled.json and Mods/install.txt to your script directory and they will be used next time the script is run (run ./manage-tModLoaderServer.sh --mods-only to install mods immediately).

## Installing Mods Immediately

Run ./manage-tModLoaderServer.sh install-mods to install the mods on your server for the management script version.

The workshop IDs should be listed one per line in the install.txt file, and corresponding mod names should be included in the enabled.json file to control which mods are actually enabled on the server.

## Available API Endpoints

While not an actual "API", uMod provides JSON endpoints for plugin search and individual plugin data, such as: https://umod.org/plugins/search.json and https://umod.org/plugins/Vanish.json

## Static Manifest API

Every plugin source has 3 endpoints including https://assets.umod.org/manifest.json, https://assets.umod.org/plugins.json, and https://assets.umod.org/plugins/manifest.json

The majority of data available has been moved to a static manifest to improve performance/availability, and the static manifest includes critical data points like dependencies and a master list that the Search API does not

## Search and Legacy API

The legacy API is paginated and searchable through endpoints like https://umod.org/plugins/search.json with parameters for query, page, sort, filter, categories, and author

## Plugin-to-Plugin Data Access

For accessing data between plugins within uMod itself, the Placeholder API plugin allows querying data about other plugins in a fast, convenient, centralized way

The search results indicate that while a formal REST API documentation may be limited, uMod provides JSON endpoints and a static manifest system for accessing plugin information.

## API Key Characteristics

All users and games are issued an API key which must be included when querying the API. It is quick and easy to use but limited to read-only GET requests, due to the limited security it offers.

## Rate Limiting

The mod.io API implements rate limiting based on the type of credentials used:

- API keys linked to a game have unlimited requests
- API keys linked to a user have 60 requests per minute
- User tokens are limited to 120 requests per minute

mod.io implements rate limiting to stop users abusing the service. Exceeding the rate limit will result in requests receiving a 429 Too Many Requests response until the reset time is reached.

## Third-Party Authentication

It is a requirement of the Game Terms with mod.io, and the platforms mod.io is used on, to ensure the user provides consent and has agreed to the latest mod.io Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. The users agreement must be collected prior to using a 3rd party authentication flow (including but not limited to Steam, PSN, Nintendo and Xbox Live).

## What is the Project Distribution Toggle?

The project distribution toggle allows each project owner to choose if the project can be distributed over 3rd party services. The project distribution toggle provides authors control over their intellectual property and revenue generated from their awesome creations.

## How It Works

If you turn this option off, any 3rd-party service, website or client will not have access to your projects or files via the 3rd-party API. Conversely, if you turn this option on any download from the 3rd party service will not count towards your total downloads nor towards your Reward Program earnings.

## API Impact

Authors' consent and the impact on earnings were solved by releasing a toggle that enables creators to choose whether or not they want to allow distribution of their mods outside of the CurseForge ecosystem. When authors opt out of third-party distribution, the API returns null values for download URLs from external sources, effectively preventing third-party launchers (like MultiMC, PolyMC, and GDLauncher) from accessing those projects.

## Managing Your Settings

You can edit this toggle by entering the project page > 'License tab', where you can view or change the distribution setting.

The toggle is part of the new CurseForge API, and determines if 3rd party developers can or cannot distribute your project information and files. What does this mean for authors? ## Sandbox_config.sbc Mod Configuration

Every world save carries its own mod list in Sandbox_config.sbc inside that world's folder, in exactly the same ModItem format. 

### ModItem Structure

Mods go in Sandbox_config.sbc in the <Mods> block with fields including FriendlyName, Name, PublishedFileId, and PublishedServiceName. Here's an example structure:

PublishedServiceName is written Steam with a capital S. Get it wrong and the mod is dropped without an error.

### Multiple Mod Services

The ModItem includes PublishedFileId and PublishedServiceName fields, indicating support for different service names like Steam. While the search results primarily show Steam as the PublishedServiceName, they don't explicitly mention mod.io in the configuration examples found.

### Auto-Download and Dependencies

Steam mods download can have difficulty when too many mods need to download for the first time, so it's recommended to add only one mod for an easy test and add one at a time later.

### Important Settings

Mods load from top to bottom in the file - the bottom one wins. In-game mod list works the opposite way where the top has highest priority. In practice, put frameworks and dependencies at the top, and mods meant to override something at the bottom.
